_source: The 3D voxel battlefield's tunables (user 2026-10-13: stop hiding them in code) — surfaced on the voxel_terrain scene object (voxelTerrain component overrides shape per scene); the values here are the historical defaults (regression pin: byte-identical field output).
shapeNotes: baseHeight = floor height (cells); rollingAmp = fBm hill amplitude; ridgeAmp/ridgePower = sharp mountain ridge height/curve; heightMin = floor clamp (top clamp is H-10, constants); grassMax = max grass cap thickness (1..grassMax cells); dirtBand/darkBand = BASE strata band thickness below the grass cap — the effective per-column thickness is wobbled by .strataWobble (DEEPEN-1015 R4); dirt fills the rest to y=0 (DEEPEN-1015: the old grey rock base band below the dark band was removed — rock/rockDark appear only via the rock scatter).
landscapeNotes: W5 architecture flip (user 2026-10-13): the voxelTerrain scene component is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the 3D terrain. These are the REAL landscape-knob defaults — byte-identical to the historical surface (regression pin). Knob -> physics mapping: bumpiness scales the rolling fBm hill amplitude (rollingAmp * bumpiness/20; 20 = identity, 0 = flat rolling, 100 = 5x); slope scales the mountain-ridge amplitude (ridgeAmp * slope/20; 20 = identity); flattenPeaks caps ridge amplitude at half its full height when on (prevents crags; off = identity); mountainPercent shifts the ridge-presence threshold ((pct - 20)/20 added to the fbm ridge noise; 20 = identity — the historical ridge density, 0 = no mountains, 100 = ridges everywhere). The settings rows (physics-presets landscape) are WRITE-THROUGH controllers onto the voxelTerrain object; the generator never reads settings.
materialsNotes: Index 0 is EMPTY (not listed). hardness scales blast resistance (0..1); color is the mesh color (hex). rockDark (P3 SETTLE-PACE-1015) is the strata shade of rock — the generator picks rock vs rockDark per cell via the depth-band rule in .rockBanding so crater cross-sections read stone-in-dirt, not tinted dirt.
strataWobbleNotes: DEEPEN-1015 R4 (user: dirt/dark strata layer thickness is uniform — randomize per-column with seeded noise): the dirt/dark band thicknesses in .shape are the BASE values; the effective thickness per column is base + round((noise2(seed ^ salt, x*freq, z*freq)*2-1) * wobble) clamped to >= 1 — a separate salt per band (dirt/dark), sampled per column x/z from the same deterministic value-noise lattice as everything else (same seed => same field, byte-identical). wobble 0 = byte-identical to the uniform-band legacy fill (regression pin). dirt/dark = amplitude in cells (integers >= 0); freq = noise lattice frequency (number > 0). Only MATERIAL bands move — geometry (solid cells) is untouched.
corridorSolidNotes: DEEPEN-1015 R4 (user: intro corridor terrain reads HOLLOW during the fall): root cause = the greedy mesher culls same-material interior faces, so when adjacent corridor chunk groups fall at staggered offsets (live-probed: up to 5 world units apart mid-fall), the seams between them expose culled interiors — see-through terrain. Fix: at slab-boundary z planes (every .corridorSolid.slabCells cells, strictly inside the corridor beyond the trench back face), the mesher emits the interior boundary faces of BOTH neighboring chunks, so every falling slab reads solid across its cross-section. slabCells = the welded fall-slab width in cells (intro_flyover groups the corridor chunk buckets by the same slab grid — the seams that can open are exactly the planes with faces); must be a positive integer multiple of the chunk size CH=32. 256 cells = 8 chunk buckets per slab (the 58-bucket corridor falls as 8 welded slabs sweeping far-to-near).
trenchNotes: DEEPEN-1015 R3 (2026-10-16): the front trench carve is a HAIRLINE band, CHUNK-ALIGNED — aquarium.js carveFrontTrench empties world z >= CAGE_Z_MAX only down to CAGE_Z_MAX + trench.trenchWorldDepth (2 world units = 8 cells at V=0.25; the back face lands exactly on the chunk-14 boundary at cellZ 448 so the falling corridor is clean whole chunks). The hairline keeps the mesher's boundary faces on BOTH sides of the slit (the cut-strata face at cellZ 439 and the corridor's first row at 448) so nothing shows holes after the drop, and the corridor surface CONTINUES the play surface with no visible step (both sides come from the SAME surfaceHeight lattice; unit-pinned in test/unit/aquarium.test.js a5). The boundary ALSO excludes trees: treeProp.js scatteredTrees clamps the scatter zMax to trenchExtent().zMax — no trees over the intro corridor / carved moat (they would sit in the air when the corridor drops). trenchWorldDepth is data with fail-noisy validation in aquarium.js — no silent default.
floorExtensionNotes: DEEPEN-1015 R6 (user 2026-10-16: 'I JUST WANT THE VOXELS TO EXTEND DOWN FURTHER' — the separate under-field MESH object is retired): the field grows DEEPER by .floorExtension.floorCells cells x V=0.25 world units below the unchanged playable floor plane: cell y=0 is now at world y = -floorCells*V, the playable floor plane stays world y=0 (cell FLOOR_CELLS), and surfaceHeight/playable tops/cage/gameplay heights are UNCHANGED (byte-identical surface law). The generator fills the deep cells with the SAME strata law (below-dark = dirt to the new floor). R6b (user: 'it keeps crashing'): 520 cells made the cells array a SINGLE 3.12 GB Uint8Array (1920*2280*712) — this Chromium's renderer crashes on multi-gigabyte single buffers (the same failure class as the medium-map 'Array buffer allocation failed'); 200 cells (50 world units, 1.72 GB array) boots clean. maxFieldBytes = the allocation budget for the cells array (fail-noisy: makeField throws a named RangeError when W*H*Z exceeds it instead of a cryptic ArrayBuffer RangeError — medium/large sizes exceed it and fail loud). Raising floorCells beyond ~200 REQUIRES splitting the cells storage into per-y-slab buffers first (field.js makeField) so no single multi-GB buffer exists. Validated fail-noisy in src/voxel3d/constants.js; no JS fallback.
rockBandingNotes: P3 SETTLE-PACE-1015, depth+wobble law DEEPEN-1015 R2/R2b: rock cells pick their material by DEPTH band measured DOWN from the column's top (the same from-the-top law as the grass/dirt/dark strata — never flat world-y lines), and the band phase is WOBBLED by seeded value noise so strata thickness/edges are randomized everywhere (no uniform cadence): a rock cell is rockDark (materials[4]) iff rockBandDark(columnTop - y, x, y, z, .rockBanding, seed), with wobble = noise amplitude in cells (0 = straight depth bands). Deterministic per seed; both rocks share hardness 1.0.

classic._note: The historical surface: no shape overrides, no rock scatter (rockScatter.count 0 by absence) — byte-identical regression pin.

terrainTypesNotes: Landscape variety (task 'landscape variety') + P3 SETTLE-PACE-1015 rock redesign: named terrain types = optional .shape overrides over .shape defaults + optional .rockScatter. rockScatter: count = boulder SITES per 100,000 field columns (extents-independent density); minDepth/maxDepth = site-center depth below the column top in cells; sizeMin/sizeMax = base radius range in cells; noiseAmp = FBM silhouette perturbation fraction (r(theta,y) = baseR * (1 + amp * (fbm*2-1))); noiseFreq = boulder angular-noise frequency (lattice units); clusterChance = chance the site rolls 1-3 smaller satellite blobs offset near the parent; pebbleDensity = single/2-cell embedded nuggets per 100,000 columns (second pass, dirt VOLUME below the surface, above y=1). Scatter is a pure MATERIAL CONVERSION of existing grass/dirt/dark cells to rock/rockDark (surface cell NEVER converted — geometry, settle, and blast shape-targets unchanged; blasts meet hardness 1.0 via the existing per-material mechanism). Deterministic per terrain seed (seeded LCG + hashInt + value-noise FBM, no Math.random); default type 'classic' produces BYTE-IDENTICAL output to the pre-feature generator. Consumed via generate(seed, { terrainType, rockAmount }); unknown names fail LOUD.
